clinical_information: Chronic headaches, recent change in character
comparison: Brain MRI without and with contrast XX/XX/2019
technique: Multisequence, multiplanar MR of the brain obtained without and with intravenous contrast. Contrast type, dose and administration as documented in electronic medical record.

Extra-axial/meninges: No extra-axial fluid collection. No abnormal dural enhancement.

Posterior fossa/cerebellum/brainstem: Normal signal and morphology. No inferior cerebellar tonsillar herniation.

Paranasal sinuses and mastoids: Mild retained secretions in the maxillary sinuses.
Bones/soft tissues: No suspicious osseous lesion.
Incidental: Small retention cyst in the left sphenoid sinus measuring approximately 8 mm.
impression:
1. No acute intracranial abnormality identified — no diffusion restriction or acute hemorrhage.
2. Scattered tiny foci of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the supratentorial white matter (up to 3 mm), most consistent with chronic microvascular ischemic change.
3. Small retention cyst in the left sphenoid sinus (approx. 8 mm), likely incidental.

examination: MR brain with and without contrast — stroke protocol
clinical_information: Acute right hemiparesis and aphasia; last known well 3 hours prior
technique: Multisequence diffusion-weighted, perfusion-sensitive, and conventional MR imaging of the brain obtained without and with intravenous contrast. Contrast type, dose and administration as documented in electronic medical record. Time-of-flight intracranial MRA performed.
findings:
Diffusion/ADC: Acute restricted diffusion in the left MCA cortex and adjacent subcortical white matter involving the opercular/insular region, measuring approximately 2.1 x 1.8 x 1.2 cm (AP x TR x CC), consistent with acute infarction.
FLAIR/T2: Corresponding FLAIR hyperintensity in the left lateral frontal/insular cortex. Mild cortical swelling in the involved territory.
Susceptibility (GRE/SWI): Tiny foci of susceptibility blooming at the periphery of the infarct measuring up to 2–3 mm, suspicious for petechial hemorrhagic conversion.
Vessels/MRA: Time-of-flight MRA demonstrates abrupt cutoff of flow in the proximal left M1 segment consistent with occlusion. Distal M2 branches show reduced caliber and flow.
Perfusion: Relative perfusion deficit corresponding to the left MCA territory with increased time-to-peak and decreased cerebral blood flow/volume in the affected region (perfusion maps reviewed).
Midline/ventricles: No mass effect causing midline shift greater than 3 mm. Ventricles preserved for age.
Other: No extra-axial hemorrhage identified. No additional acute intracranial hemorrhage.
impression:
1. Acute infarct of the left MCA territory with restricted diffusion involving the opercular/insular cortex, measuring approximately 2.1 x 1.8 x 1.2 cm — correlates with clinical focal deficits.
2. Proximal left M1 occlusion on TOF-MRA with decreased distal flow.
3. Small peripheral susceptibility foci within the infarct compatible with petechial hemorrhagic conversion.
4. Perfusion imaging shows significant hypoperfusion of the left MCA territory. Findings are time-sensitive — correlate with clinical exam and consider urgent stroke intervention per stroke team protocols.

examination: MR brain without and with contrast
clinical_information: Known right cerebellopontine angle meningioma — surveillance imaging
comparison: Brain MRI with and without contrast XX/XX/2022
technique: Multisequence, multiplanar MR of the brain obtained without and with intravenous contrast. Contrast type, dose and administration as documented in electronic medical record.
findings:
Brain parenchyma: No acute diffusion restriction. No additional intracranial mass lesions identified apart from the known extra-axial lesion.
Extra-axial/dural-based lesion: A dural-based, well-defined enhancing mass is present at the right cerebellopontine angle measuring approximately 28 x 25 x 23 mm (AP x TR x CC). The lesion demonstrates homogeneous strong postcontrast enhancement and a thin dural tail along the adjacent petrous ridge, most consistent with meningioma. Mild surrounding T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the adjacent right cerebellar hemisphere, likely vasogenic edema, extends up to 9 mm from the lesion margin.
Mass effect/hydrocephalus: The lesion mildly effaces the adjacent cerebellar folia and indents the lateral aspect of the fourth ventricle without frank obstruction. No transependymal CSF flow to suggest acute hydrocephalus. No significant midline shift.
Cranial nerves: The internal auditory canal is patent; no definite intracanalicular extension identified. Facial and vestibulocochlear nerve assessment limited by spatial resolution.
Vessels/bones: No abnormal vascular flow voids adjacent to the lesion. Mild remodeling of the adjacent petrous bone at the site of dural attachment, unchanged from prior.
Other: No other suspicious enhancing lesions.
impression:
1. Dural-based enhancing mass at the right cerebellopontine angle consistent with meningioma, measuring approximately 28 x 25 x 23 mm.  
2. Mild surrounding vasogenic edema in the adjacent right cerebellum and mild mass effect on the lateral aspect of the fourth ventricle without obstructive hydrocephalus.  
3. Findings are similar but appear mildly increased in size compared to prior study from 02/XX/2022 — recommend correlation with prior imaging and neurosurgical consultation for consideration of treatment options.

examination: MR brain without and with contrast
clinical_information: Head trauma after fall from standing; brief loss of consciousness
technique: Multisequence MR of the brain obtained without and with intravenous contrast including susceptibility-weighted sequences. Contrast type, dose and administration as documented in electronic medical record.
findings:
Susceptibility (SWI/GRE): Left convexity crescentic extra-axial susceptibility and T1/T2 hypointense collection along the left frontoparietal convexity measuring up to 6 mm in maximal thickness, consistent with acute/subacute subdural hematoma. Scattered punctate microhemorrhages involving the corpus callosum (genu and splenium) and deep white matter, the largest approximately 4 mm, suspicious for traumatic axonal injury.
Diffusion/FLAIR: No large areas of restricted diffusion to suggest acute territorial infarct. Mild sulcal effacement adjacent to the left convexity collection without significant mass effect. No transependymal edema.
Extra-axial: No epidural hematoma identified. No subarachnoid hemorrhage identified on FLAIR or susceptibility.
Midline/ventricles: Midline structures midline without measurable shift (<2 mm). Ventricular size within expected limits.
Contrast: No abnormal leptomeningeal or nodular parenchymal enhancement. No enhancing extra-axial mass.
Other: No cranial vault fracture identified on MR sequences; correlate with CT for bony detail.
impression:
1. Left convexity subdural hematoma up to 6 mm in thickness without significant midline shift (measured <2 mm).  
2. Multiple scattered punctate susceptibility foci involving the corpus callosum and deep white matter, most consistent with traumatic axonal microhemorrhages — concerning for diffuse axonal injury.  
3. No large territorial infarct or subarachnoid hemorrhage identified. Recommend neurosurgical correlation; consider follow-up imaging per institutional trauma protocol and correlate with head CT for acute management and evaluation of skull fracture.

examination: MR brain without and with contrast
clinical_information: New-onset complex partial seizures and memory disturbance
comparison: Brain MRI without and with contrast XX/XX/2020
technique: Multisequence, multiplanar MR of the brain obtained without and with intravenous contrast including thin-slice coronal T2/FLAIR and volumetric sequences through the temporal lobes. Contrast type, dose and administration as documented in electronic medical record.
findings:
Mesial temporal lobes: Left greater than right hippocampal volume loss with increased T2/FLAIR signal within the left mesial temporal structures (left hippocampal head and body), greatest width approximately 11 mm on coronal oblique images. Findings are most suggestive of mesial temporal sclerosis/hippocampal sclerosis.
Cortex/white matter: No enhancing mass identified. No diffusion restriction.
Pituitary/sella: Small rounded mildly T2 hyperintense focus at the posterior pituitary consistent with physiologic posterior pituitary bright spot. No discrete enhancing pituitary microadenoma identified.
Vessels/other: No abnormal intracranial vascular flow voids. No abnormal leptomeningeal enhancement.
Incidental: Small pineal gland cyst measuring approximately 7 mm without nodular enhancement. Paranasal sinuses clear.
impression:
1. Left hippocampal volume loss with increased T2/FLAIR signal consistent with left mesial temporal sclerosis — imaging appearance concordant with an epileptogenic focus.  
2. No enhancing mass or acute abnormality identified.  
3. Incidental small pineal cyst measuring approximately 7 mm, likely benign.  
Recommendation: Correlate with EEG and clinical seizure semiology; consider epilepsy surgery evaluation if clinically indicated.

examination: CT chest without contrast
clinical_information: Blunt thoracic trauma after motor vehicle collision. Right-sided chest pain, shortness of breath.
technique: Axial CT images of the chest were obtained without intravenous contrast. Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.
findings:
Lungs and pleura: Small right apical and lateral pneumothorax measuring up to approximately 8 mm in thickness at the most dependent portion. Small right pleural fluid/hemorrhagic effusion layering along the lateral chest, estimated depth ~10 mm. Patchy right greater than left peripheral consolidation and ground-glass opacity consistent with pulmonary contusion, greatest in the right middle and right lower lobes, measuring up to 35 mm in greatest axial dimension. No large-volume hemothorax.
Chest wall and bones: Comminuted fractures of the right lateral 8th and 9th ribs with mild displacement; nondisplaced fracture of the right 7th rib. No sternal or clavicular fracture identified. No acute displaced fractures of the thoracic spine seen.
Mediastinum and heart: No widened mediastinum. Cardiomediastinal contours within expected limits for technique.
Additional: No subcutaneous emphysema identified. No intraparenchymal hemorrhagic contusion >2 cm.
Impression embedded within findings for clarity.
impression: 1. Small right-sided pneumothorax (maximum thickness ~8 mm). 2. Right lateral rib fractures involving the 8th and 9th ribs (comminuted, mild displacement); additional nondisplaced 7th rib fracture. 3. Small right pleural effusion, likely hemorrhagic, layering posteriorly (~10 mm). 4. Patchy pulmonary contusions in the right middle and lower lobes (largest focus ~35 mm). 5. No acute intrathoracic aortic injury or large-volume hemothorax identified. Clinical correlation recommended; consider chest tube placement for symptomatic or enlarging pneumothorax and repeat chest radiograph or CT for interval assessment.

examination: CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) of the chest with contrast
clinical_information: Acute onset dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. Elevated D-dimer, concern for pulmonary embolism.
technique: CT pulmonary angiography obtained following intravenous administration of iodinated contrast. Multiphase thin-section axial images with coronal and sagittal reformats were reviewed. Right ventricular and left ventricular short-axis measurements obtained on axial images.
findings:
Pulmonary arterial vasculature: Acute thromboembolic filling defects are present within segmental and subsegmental branches of the right lower lobe pulmonary artery and within a segmental branch of the left lower lobe. No central saddle embolus identified. No embolus seen in the main or lobar pulmonary arteries.
Cardiomediastinal: Mild right ventricular enlargement with an estimated RV/LV short-axis ratio of approximately 1.05 (measured on axial images), suggestive of mild right heart strain. No pericardial effusion.
Lungs and pleura: Patchy peripheral wedge-shaped airspace opacity at the right lower lobe periphery consistent with infarct or associated atelectasis/consolidation, measuring up to 18 x 22 mm. Small bilateral pleural effusions, greater on the right, with maximum measured thickness of 12 mm.
Other: Moderate coronary artery atherosclerotic calcification. No acute osseous abnormality.
Comparison note: Compared with prior exam XX/XX/XXXX, thrombus location appears similar in distribution (if prior positive), or if prior was negative, this is new — please correlate with comparison report.
impression: 1. Acute pulmonary emboli within segmental and subsegmental branches of the right lower lobe and a segmental branch of the left lower lobe. 2. Mild right ventricular enlargement with RV/LV ratio ~1.05, concerning for mild right heart strain. 3. Small bilateral pleural effusions, greater on the right. 4. Patchy peripheral right lower lobe airspace opacity (up to 22 mm), which may reflect pulmonary infarct or associated consolidation. 5. Incidental moderate coronary artery atherosclerotic calcification. Recommend clinical correlation and prompt anticoagulation per clinical status; consider cardiology/PE response team evaluation given signs of right heart strain.

clinical_information: Known right upper lobe lung mass; staging and restaging for neoplasm. Interval cough and weight loss.
technique: Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest performed in the venous phase following IV iodinated contrast administration. Multiplanar reconstructions reviewed.
findings:
Lungs and airways: Spiculated enhancing mass in the right upper lobe APical/posterior segment measuring approximately 2.8 x 2.6 x 2.4 cm (axial greatest dimension 28 mm). This represents interval increase compared with prior CT dated XX/XX/XXXX where the lesion measured approximately 1.6 cm. Multiple additional pulmonary nodules in the left lung, the largest measuring 9 mm in the left lower lobe and another 6 mm subpleural nodule in the left upper lobe—suspicious for metastatic disease.
Mediastinum and hila: Enlarged right paratracheal and right hilar lymph nodes with the largest short-axis measurement ~16 mm (right lower paratracheal). No bulky mediastinal adenopathy greater than 20 mm.
Pleura and pericardium: Small bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than left, estimated maximum depth 8–10 mm. No definite pleural nodularity identified on these images. No pericardial effusion.
Chest wall and bones: No overt osseous metastatic lesion identified on the included field of view.
Incidental: 1. Small heterogeneous nodule within the inferior right thyroid lobe measuring approximately 9 mm; consider correlation with dedicated neck ultrasound. 2. No acute cardiopulmonary edema.
impression: 1. Spiculated enhancing right upper lobe mass measuring 2.8 cm, interval increase from prior study on XX/XX/XXXX (prior 1.6 cm) — concerning for primary lung malignancy. 2. Right paratracheal and right hilar adenopathy (largest short axis ~16 mm), suspicious for nodal metastatic disease. 3. Multiple small contralateral pulmonary nodules (largest ~9 mm in left lower lobe) concerning for metastatic spread. 4. Small bilateral pleural effusions (right > left). 5. Incidental 9 mm right thyroid lobe nodule — consider ultrasound correlation. Recommend PET/CT for further staging and tissue diagnosis (bronchoscopy or CT-guided biopsy) as clinically appropriate.

comparison: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast XX/XX/XXXX
technique: Multiphase contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis performed following intravenous iodinated contrast (type and dose documented in electronic medical record). Portal venous phase images reviewed with axial, coronal and sagittal reformats.
findings:
Liver: Multiple hypoenhancing hepatic lesions scattered throughout both lobes suspicious for metastatic disease. The largest lesion is in segment VII measuring approximately 4.2 x 3.8 cm. Several smaller lesions measured: 2.1 cm (segment IV), 1.4 cm (segment II), and numerous subcentimeter lesions. Compared with prior study dated XX/XX/XXXX there is interval increase in size and number of hepatic lesions.
Lymph nodes: Enlarged porta hepatis and periportal lymph nodes measuring up to 2.5 x 1.8 cm. Several subcentimeter retroperitoneal nodes are present.
Bowel/primary site: Postoperative changes in the left lower quadrant at the expected surgical bed; no evidence of locally recurrent mass identified on current images.
Osseous structures: No lytic destructive osseous metastases identified on this exam; limited sensitivity.
Pelvis: Complex left adnexal cystic mass measures approximately 5.0 x 4.5 cm with internal septations and heterogeneous density—could represent hemorrhagic/complex functional cyst versus cystic metastasis; correlation with pelvic ultrasound or clinical history suggested. No frank pelvic free fluid.
Other solid organs: Spleen, pancreas and kidneys demonstrate no focal suspicious lesions apart from subcentimeter renal cysts.
No bowel obstruction or pneumoperitoneum.
impression: 1. Multiple hepatic metastases, largest in segment VII measuring 4.2 x 3.8 cm; interval increase in size and number of hepatic lesions compared with prior exam XX/XX/XXXX—worrisome for progression. 2. Enlarged porta hepatis lymphadenopathy up to 2.5 cm. 3. Complex left adnexal cystic mass measuring ~5.0 x 4.5 cm—recommend pelvic ultrasound correlation to further characterize and to evaluate for possible metastatic disease. 4. No acute bowel obstruction or free intraperitoneal air identified. Recommend multidisciplinary discussion for management given interval progression of hepatic metastatic disease.

examination: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast (trauma protocol)
clinical_information: Blunt abdominal trauma after motor vehicle collision, hypotension in field
technique: Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest/abdomen/pelvis following intravenous iodinated contrast (type and dose documented in electronic medical record). Arterial and portal venous phase images obtained with multiplanar reconstructions.
findings:
Spleen: Irregular splenic laceration along the lateral superior pole measuring approximately 3.5 cm in greatest depth. Subcapsular and perisplenic hematoma is present measuring up to 4.5 x 3.0 cm. There is focal intraparenchymal contrast extravasation on arterial phase with pooling on portal venous phase consistent with active hemorrhage.
Liver: Small subcapsular hepatic contusion along the superior surface measuring up to 1.2 cm; no active extravasation identified in the liver.
Kidneys/adrenals: No renal laceration or active urinary extravasation identified.
Bowel/mesentery: No pneumoperitoneum to suggest bowel perforation. No focal mesenteric vascular injury identified.
Thorax (included portions): Small left hemothorax with trace layering dependent pleural fluid. No large pneumothorax identified.
Osseous: Acute fracture of the left 9th and 10th ribs posteriorly.
Other: Moderate volume hemoperitoneum layering in the dependent pelvis and perisplenic region.
impression: 1. Splenic laceration with associated subcapsular/perisplenic hematoma and active intraparenchymal contrast extravasation—findings consistent with ongoing splenic hemorrhage (urgent). 2. Moderate hemoperitoneum. 3. Small subcapsular hepatic contusion without active extravasation. 4. Left-sided rib fractures (9th and 10th) and small left hemothorax. Recommendation: Immediate surgical and/or interventional radiology consultation for management of splenic hemorrhage; correlate with hemodynamic status and serial hemoglobin levels.

examination: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV and oral contrast
clinical_information: Left lower quadrant pain, history of acute sigmoid diverticulitis treated conservatively 6 weeks ago
comparison: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast XX/XX/XXXX
technique: CT with oral and IV iodinated contrast agent (type and dose documented in electronic medical record). Portal venous phase images with multiplanar reformats.
findings:
Colon: Wall thickening and mural hyperenhancement of the distal sigmoid colon with pericolic fat stranding consistent with active/inflammatory change. A small pericolic fluid collection adjacent to the sigmoid measured approximately 1.0 x 0.8 cm. Compared with prior exam dated XX/XX/XXXX the previously reported 2.5 cm adjacent collection is decreased in size. No air-fluid level or rim-enhancing collection identified to suggest a mature drainable abscess.
Bowel/obstruction: No evidence of small or large bowel obstruction. No pneumoperitoneum.
Solid organs: Incidental simple hepatic cyst in segment VI measuring 1.8 cm. Liver, spleen, pancreas and kidneys otherwise unremarkable for acute process.
Lymph nodes: No suspicious bulky lymphadenopathy.
Other: No free intraperitoneal gas. Minimal dependent pelvic free fluid.
impression: 1. Findings compatible with resolving sigmoid diverticulitis: persistent sigmoid wall thickening and pericolic inflammatory change. 2. Interval decrease in adjacent pericolic fluid collection from 2.5 cm on prior exam (XX/XX/XXXX) to ~1.0 cm on current study; no drainable rim-enhancing abscess identified. 3. No bowel obstruction or pneumoperitoneum. 4. Incidental simple hepatic cyst in segment VI measuring ~1.8 cm. Recommendation: Continue conservative management and clinical follow-up; consider repeat imaging if symptoms worsen or fail to improve.
